page: Microsoft Azure M16bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The configuration features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. It includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a 410 GB local disk, and the instance is premium storage capable, allowing for high-performance block storage attachments. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2196.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 32.97 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is characterized as average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 13388.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 16883.26. Memory bandwidth tests show 107.61 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 68.03 GB/sec for large block write operations. In database and key-value operations, the server achieved 22.55 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and a Passmark database score of 9124.59.

Given the dedicated Intel Xeon processor and high vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the M16bds_v3 offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The inclusion of local storage and premium storage capability makes it highly suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing, and medium-scale software compilation. It is also capable of handling light LLM inference workloads, processing up to 303.34 tokens per second for small models.
